samples.summary: No end-to-end test of the logged-in success path for `status` or `ctx list`
samples.evidence: The new `status / ctx list command wiring` describe block always points `WAFFLEBASE_SESSION` at `/nonexistent/wafflebase-session.json` (beforeEach, status.test.ts:~90), so every wired test exercises only the logged-out / error branches: default JSON logged-out, csv logged-out, INVALID_FORMAT, NOT_LOGGED_IN. The success path through `output(buildWorkspaceList(...), fmt, opts.quiet)` in ctx.ts:79-83 and `output(buildStatus(loadSession()), ...)` with a real session is never driven end-to-end — nothing would catch, e.g., the payload being printed to stderr, wrong exit code, or `opts.format` not being threaded on the success branch. A test could write a temp session file via saveSession and run `ctx list`.

samples.summary: `formatRecord`'s `?? ''` null/undefined fallback is untested although `buildStatus` can emit `workspaceName: null`
samples.evidence: table.ts:13 renders `String(record[k] ?? '')`. buildStatus (status.ts) returns `workspaceName: null` when the active workspace is missing from the session list, and the table test 'renders every field under --format table' (status.test.ts) uses a session where the workspace resolves, so the null value never reaches formatRecord. output.test.ts's new key/value tests use `{ loggedIn: true, user: 'hackerwins' }` only. Nothing asserts a null field renders as blank rather than 'null'.

samples.summary: Test titled 'renders every field under --format table' asserts only 3 of the 8 payload fields
samples.evidence: The test checks `toContain('hackerwins')`, `toContain('http://localhost:3000')`, `toContain('valid')` and `not.toContain('[object Object]')`. It does not assert email, workspaceId, workspaceName, expiresAt or loggedIn appear, so a regression that dropped keys from the record renderer (or from buildStatus) for those fields would still pass despite the title's claim of full coverage.

samples.summary: Changed `status` / `ctx.list` schema response shapes have no test tying them to the actual payloads
samples.evidence: registry.ts:63-80 now advertises the new status field set and the ctx.list `{id,name,active}` item shape. packages/cli/test/schema.test.ts asserts only names, safety levels, alias resolution and a couple of docs params — nothing compares the declared `response` keys against `buildStatus(...)` / `buildWorkspaceList(...)` output, so registry drift from the real payloads (the exact bug this PR fixes for ctx.list) would go undetected again.

samples.summary: `--quiet` is not exercised through the new command wiring
samples.evidence: Both new actions pass `opts.quiet` into `output`/`outputError`, but no wiring test runs e.g. `['status','--quiet']` to assert stdout is silent and exit code stays 0, nor `['ctx','list','--quiet']` to assert exit 1 with no stderr. Only the unit-level `outputError('...', true)` case in output.test.ts:183 covers quiet, so mis-threading `opts.quiet` in the commands would not be caught.
